entries.name: ACE-Step 1.5
entries.use_for: Generate full songs locally from text with an open music model, via UI, Python or REST API.
entries.why: Runs under 4GB VRAM and trains a style LoRA from a few songs.
entries.summary: An open-source music foundation model that generates full songs on consumer hardware. It ships a Gradio UI, Python API, REST API, CLI and a VST3 plugin. Supports CUDA, MPS, ROCm, Intel XPU and CPU.
entries.best_for: Adding local AI music generation to an app or workflow without a paid API, including personalised styles via LoRA.
entries.not_for: Machines with no GPU if you need speed. The XL models need 12GB VRAM or more, and Python must be 3.11 or 3.12.

entries.name: audio.cpp
entries.use_for: Run text-to-speech, speech-to-text, voice conversion and music models locally from one C++ runtime.
entries.why: No Python needed, and one native runtime supports 100+ audio model architectures on NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and CPU.
entries.summary: A C++ audio inference framework on ggml. It runs TTS, STT, VAD, voice conversion and music generation models with a CLI and server, on Windows, Linux and macOS, with GGUF models on Hugging Face and streaming for several TTS models.
entries.best_for: Apps that want local, portable audio AI without Python dependencies.
entries.not_for: Each model has its own requirements and options, so read the model docs. The license is not clearly stated.

entries.name: AudioKit
entries.use_for: Audio synthesis, processing and analysis for iOS and macOS apps
entries.why: The main Swift audio framework: oscillators, effects, sequencing and analysis on top of AVAudioEngine.
entries.summary: Swift audio synthesis, processing and analysis platform for iOS, macOS and tvOS with oscillators, effects, sequencing and a Cookbook of examples.
entries.best_for: Apple-platform apps with synthesis, effects or audio analysis.
entries.not_for: Apple platforms only; not for cross-platform or web audio.

entries.name: AudioNoise
entries.use_for: Read small, simple digital audio effect code built from IIR filters and delay loops.
entries.why: Tiny sample-in, sample-out effects written to learn DSP basics.
entries.summary: A set of toy digital audio effects from a guitar-pedal project. It uses only IIR filters and basic delay loops, with single-sample processing and no added latency, to explore digital audio basics.
entries.best_for: Learning basic DSP effect code and how low-latency per-sample processing looks.
entries.not_for: The author calls these toy effects not to be taken seriously. GPL-2.0, and not a polished effects library.

entries.name: DawDreamer
entries.use_for: Render audio with VST instruments, effects and Faust from Python scripts.
entries.why: Scriptable DAW engine for batch rendering and ML dataset generation.
entries.summary: Python digital audio workstation framework that renders audio graphs with VST instruments/effects and Faust DSP scripts offline.
entries.best_for: Scripted audio rendering, plugin automation and dataset generation in Python.
entries.not_for: Offline-oriented; not a live audio engine or GUI DAW.

entries.name: Essentia
entries.use_for: Audio analysis and music information retrieval with C++, Python and JS/WASM
entries.why: Rich MIR toolkit (key, tempo, features, models) from the UPF Music Technology Group.
entries.summary: C++ audio analysis and music information retrieval library with Python bindings and JS/WASM, with many spectral, tonal and rhythm descriptors and pretrained models.
entries.best_for: Music analysis tasks such as tempo, key, features and tagging.
entries.not_for: AGPLv3 license, a caveat for closed-source use; heavier to build than librosa.

entries.name: Faust
entries.use_for: Functional DSP language that compiles to C++, WASM, plugins and more
entries.why: Write DSP once and target VST/AU, web and embedded; LGPL-2.1+ compiler.
entries.summary: Functional programming language for real-time signal processing that compiles DSP programs to C++, C, Java, LLVM, WebAssembly, plugins and more.
entries.best_for: Writing DSP and synth/effects once and exporting to many targets.
entries.not_for: Needs learning a DSP-specific language; compiler tool rather than a ready-made audio app.

entries.name: FluidSynth
entries.use_for: Real-time SoundFont 2 software synthesizer, usable as a library or CLI
entries.why: The go-to way to turn MIDI into sound with SoundFonts; embedded in many apps.
entries.summary: Real-time software synthesizer for SoundFont 2 files, usable as a library or CLI, with MIDI input and cross-platform support.
entries.best_for: Playing MIDI with SoundFont instruments in apps, games or on the command line.
entries.not_for: Sample-based SoundFont synthesis only; not a general synth design environment.

entries.name: HeartMuLa
entries.use_for: Generate music from lyrics and style tags with open-source models.
entries.why: A full open family: music model, codec, lyrics transcriber and audio-text alignment.
entries.summary: A family of open music models. HeartMuLa generates music from lyrics and tags in many languages, HeartCodec is a 12.5 Hz codec, HeartTranscriptor transcribes lyrics, and HeartCLAP aligns audio and text. A script runs generation from the command line.
entries.best_for: Developers who want a local, open alternative for lyrics-to-song generation.
entries.not_for: Needs a GPU with enough memory (lazy loading helps on one card). The strongest 7B version is not the released one.

entries.name: howler.js
entries.use_for: Simple cross-browser audio playback for the web (Web Audio with HTML5 fallback)
entries.why: The default web audio playback library for games and apps; tiny and dependable.
entries.stable_reason: Mature, feature-complete Web Audio/HTML5 playback wrapper; API stable for years and widely depended on
entries.summary: JavaScript audio library defaulting to Web Audio API with HTML5 Audio fallback, handling cross-browser quirks, sprites, grouping and caching.
entries.best_for: Games and websites needing simple reliable audio playback.
entries.not_for: Playback-focused; Tone.js is better for synthesis and sequencing, and the repo is lightly maintained.

entries.name: JUCE
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform audio apps and VST/AU/AAX plugins in C++.
entries.why: Industry standard for audio plugin development; AGPLv3 or commercial license.
entries.summary: C++ framework for desktop and mobile apps and audio plug-ins (VST, VST3, AU, AAX, LV2), with CMake and Projucer project generation.
entries.best_for: Building commercial audio plugins and audio applications in C++.
entries.not_for: Dual-licensed; paid or restricted terms for closed-source commercial use; heavy for non-audio apps.

entries.name: KFR
entries.use_for: Do high-performance DSP in C++: FFT, filters and sample-rate conversion.
entries.why: SIMD-optimized DSP framework with fast FFT; GPL or commercial license.
entries.summary: C++ DSP framework with high-performance FFT, filters, convolution and sample-rate conversion. Dual-licensed GPLv2+ or commercial.
entries.best_for: Performance-critical C++ DSP code.
entries.not_for: GPLv2+ unless you buy a commercial license; C++ only.

entries.name: librosa
entries.use_for: Analyze music and audio in Python: spectrograms, beats, pitch and features.
entries.why: The standard Python library for music information retrieval and audio features.
entries.summary: Python library for audio and music analysis providing spectrograms, beat tracking, pitch, features and loading utilities as building blocks for MIR.
entries.best_for: Audio feature extraction and ML preprocessing in Python.
entries.not_for: Analysis-only and offline; not for real-time audio or plugins.

entries.name: libsndfile
entries.use_for: Read and write WAV, FLAC, Ogg and other sampled audio file formats
entries.why: Foundational audio file I/O used by Audacity, python-soundfile and more.
entries.summary: C library for reading and writing sampled audio files such as WAV, FLAC and Ogg.
entries.best_for: Reading/writing audio file formats from C/C++ programs.
entries.not_for: File I/O only: no playback, DSP or MP3 beyond what formats it supports.

entries.name: LuxTTS
entries.use_for: Clone a voice from a short sample and generate 48kHz speech very fast on a local GPU or CPU.
entries.why: Runs at over 150x realtime and fits in about 1GB of VRAM.
entries.summary: LuxTTS is a small text-to-speech model built on ZipVoice for voice cloning. It outputs 48kHz audio, runs on CUDA, MPS and CPU, and takes a reference audio file of at least 3 seconds.
entries.best_for: Local, low-resource voice cloning and TTS where speed matters.
entries.not_for: Streaming production services: the README roadmap still lists v1.5 and float16 code as to-do. Cloning needs a clean reference clip.

entries.name: miniaudio
entries.use_for: Single-file C library for audio playback, capture, decoding and mixing
entries.why: Zero-dependency cross-platform audio layer used by raylib and many engines.

license_verified.note: LICENSE: dual public domain (Unlicense) or MIT No Attribution, user's choice

entries.summary: Single-file C library for audio playback, capture, decoding and mixing with no dependencies and broad platform support.
entries.best_for: Embedding cross-platform audio I/O in games or apps with minimal setup.
entries.not_for: Low-level engine; no high-level music or synth features.

entries.name: Miso TTS
entries.use_for: Generate emotive, conversational English speech locally from text using an 8B text-to-dialogue model.
entries.why: An 8B RVQ Transformer in the Sesame CSM style, tuned for high-quality conversational speech.
entries.summary: An 8 billion parameter text-to-dialogue model that generates Mimi audio codes from text and optional audio context, using a Llama 3.2-style backbone. The repo holds inference code, the model definition and setup for running it locally.
entries.best_for: Trying or integrating a highly expressive open TTS model for dialogue.
entries.not_for: English only. An 8B model needs a capable GPU. The license is not stated in the README excerpt, so check it before commercial use.

entries.name: MOSS-TTS Family
entries.use_for: Generate long-form speech, multi-speaker dialogue, designed voices and sound effects.
entries.why: Five models that work alone or together, with fine control over pinyin, phonemes and duration.
entries.summary: An open speech and sound generation family. It includes MOSS-TTS for zero-shot cloning and long speech, MOSS-TTSD for dialogue, VoiceGenerator for voice design, SoundEffect and a real-time streaming model. Demo scripts are included.
entries.best_for: Production-style speech apps needing cloning, dialogue or voice design, with model weights you control.
entries.not_for: The larger models need GPU resources. For a tiny CPU model use MOSS-TTS-Nano instead.

entries.name: MOSS-TTS-Nano
entries.use_for: Add real-time multilingual text-to-speech and voice cloning that runs on CPU.
entries.why: A 0.1B model with streaming output that runs on a 4-core CPU.
entries.summary: A tiny open speech model using an audio tokenizer plus an LLM. It outputs 48 kHz stereo, supports many languages, streaming, long text with voice cloning, and ONNX CPU inference. Includes an Android ONNX example.
entries.best_for: Local demos, web serving or on-device apps that need speech without a GPU.
entries.not_for: A small model, so quality trails larger TTS systems. Check the model card for supported languages and limits.

entries.name: music21
entries.use_for: Toolkit for symbolic music: parse, analyze and generate scores, MIDI and MusicXML
entries.why: The standard for computational musicology and symbolic music generation.
entries.summary: Python toolkit for computational musicology: parse, analyze, create and convert symbolic music such as scores, MIDI and MusicXML.
entries.best_for: Symbolic music analysis, corpus studies and score generation.
entries.not_for: Works on notation, not audio signals; can be slow on large corpora.

entries.name: NeuTTS
entries.use_for: Run open text-to-speech models on-device with instant voice cloning from a few seconds of audio.
entries.why: Small LM-plus-codec speech models in GGUF form that run on laptops, phones and Raspberry Pis.
entries.summary: A family of on-device TTS models (Air, Nano in several languages, 2E with emotion control) built on LLM backbones. Quantized GGUF builds are provided, and a 3-second reference clip is enough to clone a voice.
entries.best_for: Private or offline voice agents, toys and embedded apps that need natural speech.
entries.not_for: Cloud-scale serving. Non-English backbones need care, and voice cloning raises consent concerns. The license is not clearly stated.

entries.name: OmniVoice
entries.use_for: Generate speech in 600+ languages with zero-shot voice cloning or voice design.
entries.why: Broadest language coverage of zero-shot TTS models, running about 40 times faster than real time.
entries.summary: OmniVoice is a massively multilingual zero-shot text-to-speech model with a diffusion language model-style design. It clones a voice from reference audio or designs one from attributes such as gender, age, pitch and accent. It offers a Python API, command-line tools, a web demo and training code.
entries.best_for: Multilingual TTS or voice cloning in your own Python app.
entries.not_for: Voice design in most languages. It is trained on Chinese and English only, and voice cloning is the most stable mode.

entries.name: Pedalboard
entries.use_for: Apply studio-quality effects and VST/AU plugins to audio in Python.
entries.why: Spotify fast JUCE-based library; reads/writes audio and runs plugins from Python (GPL-3.0).
entries.summary: Python library for audio file I/O and effects, with built-in effects and support for loading VST3 and Audio Unit plugins, built by Spotify.
entries.best_for: Applying studio effects and plugins in Python pipelines and ML data augmentation.
entries.not_for: Not a real-time DAW; plugin hosting depends on platform.

entries.name: Pocket TTS
entries.use_for: Generate speech from text on a CPU with a pip install and a function call.
entries.why: 100M parameters, about 6x real-time on a laptop CPU, with voice cloning.
entries.summary: A small text-to-speech model and Python package from Kyutai. It streams audio with about 200ms to the first chunk, uses two CPU cores, clones voices and supports seven languages. It has a CLI and can run in the browser. Training code is available.
entries.best_for: Apps and agents that need local, low-latency TTS with no GPU.
entries.not_for: Top-tier studio voice quality or languages beyond the seven listed. It needs PyTorch 2.5 or newer.

entries.name: pydub
entries.use_for: Manipulate audio (cut, concat, effects, convert) with a simple Python API
entries.why: The easiest Python audio-editing API, built on ffmpeg.
entries.stable_reason: Small, finished ffmpeg-backed audio manipulation API; behaviour stable for years
entries.summary: Python library with a simple API to slice, concatenate, convert, and apply basic effects to audio, using ffmpeg for most formats.
entries.best_for: Quick scripts for editing and converting audio files.
entries.not_for: Basic operations only; not for heavy DSP or real-time use, and needs ffmpeg for non-WAV.

entries.name: Q Audio DSP
entries.use_for: Build audio effects and synths with a modern C++ DSP library.
entries.why: Clean C++ DSP building blocks including pitch detection, MIT licensed.
entries.summary: Modern C++ audio DSP library emphasizing simple, functional-style design, efficient enough for microcontrollers.
entries.best_for: Writing audio effects and synths in modern C++, including embedded.
entries.not_for: C++ only and smaller ecosystem than JUCE or Faust.

entries.name: SAM-Audio
entries.use_for: Isolate a specific sound from an audio mix using a text, visual or time-span prompt.
entries.why: Meta's Segment Anything idea for audio, with three prompt types.
entries.summary: Inference code and checkpoints for a model that separates sounds from complex audio. You describe the sound in text, point at objects in video, or give time spans. A Python API loads the model from Hugging Face.
entries.best_for: Audio and video tools that need prompt-driven sound isolation.
entries.not_for: Checkpoints need access approval on Hugging Face and a GPU. The license is not a standard open one, so read it first.

entries.name: Sonic Pi
entries.use_for: Make music by live coding with a Ruby-based language and SuperCollider synths.
entries.why: The most popular music live-coding environment, used widely in education and performance.
entries.summary: Live-coding music environment with a Ruby-based language and SuperCollider synths, for creating and performing music through code.
entries.best_for: Learning programming through music and live-coding performance.
entries.not_for: A standalone app, not an embeddable library.

entries.name: SoundCraft
entries.use_for: Recording, editing and mixing multitrack audio with a full mixer, MIDI editor and automation, like Pro Tools.
entries.why: Runs natively on macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD and in the browser via WebAssembly, and is fully scriptable.
entries.summary: SoundCraft is a clean-room, open-source digital audio workstation written in pure Rust, following the Edit/Mix window workflow of Avid Pro Tools. It supports multitrack editing, a full mixer with plugins and automation, a MIDI editor with built-in synths, video playback, and command-line or AI-agent scripting of every action.
entries.best_for: Developers or studios wanting an open, scriptable, cross-platform DAW instead of a closed commercial one.
entries.not_for: Not for users who need compatibility with existing Pro Tools sessions or third-party plugin formats it doesn't support.

entries.name: SpeechBrain
entries.use_for: PyTorch toolkit for speech recognition, enhancement and speaker tasks
entries.why: All-in-one speech toolkit with pretrained recipes for ASR, separation, diarization and enhancement.
entries.summary: PyTorch toolkit for speech and conversational AI: ASR, speech enhancement, speaker recognition, TTS and more, with recipes and pretrained models.
entries.best_for: Training or fine-tuning speech models in PyTorch.
entries.not_for: Research-oriented and PyTorch-only.

entries.name: Spleeter
entries.use_for: Separate songs into vocal, drum, bass and other stems.
entries.why: Deezer pretrained separation models, fast and simple to use from CLI or Python.
entries.summary: Deezer's TensorFlow library with pretrained models to separate music into stems such as vocals, drums and bass.
entries.best_for: Quick vocal and instrument stem separation.
entries.not_for: Older TensorFlow-based project; newer models often outperform it.

entries.name: SuperCollider
entries.use_for: Real-time audio synthesis server and language for algorithmic composition
entries.why: The classic sound-synthesis engine that TidalCycles, Sonic Pi and others build on.
entries.summary: Platform for audio synthesis and algorithmic composition with scsynth real-time server, supernova multicore server and sclang language.
entries.best_for: Experimental synthesis, generative music and sound art.
entries.not_for: Steep learning curve; custom client/server architecture and language.

entries.name: Tone.js
entries.use_for: Build interactive music, synths and sequencers in the browser on the Web Audio API.
entries.why: The standard web music framework with scheduling, instruments and effects.
entries.summary: Web Audio framework for interactive music in the browser, with a transport for scheduling, prebuilt synths and effects, and audio building blocks.
entries.best_for: Browser-based synths, sequencers and interactive music.
entries.not_for: Web Audio only, so browser or JS runtimes; not for simple sound-effect playback.

entries.name: torchaudio
entries.use_for: Load, transform and augment audio for PyTorch models.
entries.why: Official PyTorch audio library with GPU-accelerated transforms and I/O.
entries.summary: PyTorch library for audio I/O, transforms, datasets, augmentation and models; per its README, TorchAudio is now maintained to work with all newer torch releases.
entries.best_for: Audio preprocessing and model pipelines in PyTorch.
entries.not_for: PyTorch-bound, and the README notes some features were removed or transitioned out.

entries.name: Voicebox
entries.use_for: Clone voices, generate speech, dictate into any app and give agents a voice, all locally.
entries.why: Bundles 8 TTS engines, dictation and an MCP voice for agents in one local app.
entries.summary: Voicebox is a local-first voice studio. It clones voices from a few seconds of audio, generates speech in 23 languages across 8 TTS engines, and dictates into any text field with a global hotkey. It adds effects and a bundled local LLM for refinement.
entries.best_for: You want a private ElevenLabs and WisprFlow style tool, or a local voice for MCP agents.
entries.not_for: It is a desktop app, not a library. Auto-paste dictation on Windows and Linux is still on the roadmap.

entries.name: VoiceStudio
entries.use_for: Clone voices, dub video, dictate and make audiobooks locally, with a local API and MCP for agents.
entries.why: An offline ElevenLabs-style studio covering cloning, dubbing, dictation and audiobooks across 646 languages.
entries.summary: VoiceStudio is a desktop app for voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook creation. It defaults to the OmniVoice engine and supports others. It runs on your hardware and exposes a local API and MCP.
entries.best_for: You want a local voice toolkit, or a local TTS and dubbing API for your own tools or agents.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0, and it is an app, not an embeddable library. Quality depends on the model and your hardware. Analytics need consent.

entries.name: VoxCPM
entries.use_for: Generate speech in 30 languages, design new voices from text, or clone a voice from a short clip.
entries.why: A tokenizer-free 2B text-to-speech model with 48kHz output, voice design and streaming.
entries.summary: VoxCPM2 is a text-to-speech model that makes continuous speech with a diffusion autoregressive design instead of discrete tokens. It supports 30 languages, voice design from a description, controllable cloning and real-time streaming, via a Python API and a CLI.
entries.best_for: Apps that need high quality multilingual TTS or voice cloning you can run yourself.
entries.not_for: A 2B model needs a capable GPU for real-time use (the README quotes an RTX 4090). The README also lists risks of misuse for cloning.

entries.name: wavesurfer.js
entries.use_for: Render interactive audio waveforms with playback, regions and timelines in the browser.
entries.why: The go-to waveform library with plugins for regions, spectrograms and recording.
entries.summary: Interactive audio waveform rendering and playback library for web apps, with regions, timeline and other plugins.
entries.best_for: Waveform display and audio editing UIs in the browser.
entries.not_for: Visualization and playback only; not an audio editor or synth.
